To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Euglena EF-11 is a single-subunit protein of 56,000 molecular weight which catalyzes the binding of aminoacyl-tRNA to the acceptor sites of 70 S and 80 S ribosomal subunits and that the affinity of EF-11 for guanine nucleotide is approximately eightfold higher for GTP than for GDP.

Euglena EF- 1L catalyzes polymerizations on procaryotic, eucaryotic and organellal ribosomes, is composed of a 56,000 molecular weight subunit, is not stimulated or inhibited by E. coli elongation factor Tu, and has an affinity for GTP that is greater than its affinity for GDP.
the EF- 1 L from Euglena is the first factor of this type that has been shown to function on both prokaryotic and organellular ribosomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of a cytoplasmatic elongation factor that can function on procaryotic, organellar, and eucaryotic ribosomes.
the purification and characterization of EF-1 from Euglena gracillis, a protozoan which has the ability to synthesize proteins in the cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplast.
the purification and characterization of a single elongation factor from Euglena that catalyzes the GTP-dependent binding of aminoacyl-tRNA to ribosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Euglena EF- 1 L is a cytoplasmically located elongation factor that functions on procaryote as well as organellar ribosomes, and that is structurally and functionally similar to other eucaryotic EF-1 L s.
Euglena EF- 1L is a low-molecular-weight protein that functions on procary-otic and organellar as well as eucaryotic ribosomes.

Euglena EF- 1 L is a low-molecular-weight factor that is similar in many respects to the eucaryotic EF-1s and the procaryotic EF-Ts but is different in its ability to function on procaryotic ribosomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Euglena EF- 1 L appears to be a cytoplasmically synthesized factor which is structurally and catalytically similar to the cytoplasmically and mitochondrially synthesized EF-1s.
Euglena EF- 1 L is a single polypeptide with a molecular weight of 56,000 which functions on both eukaryotic and procaryotic ribosomes and is similar in many ways to EF-1s from other organisms.
Euglena EF- 1 L is the only factor known that can function on both prokaryotic and eukaryotic ribosomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EF- 1 L from Euglena is capable of catalyzing the binding of aminoacyl-tRNAs to both eucaryotic and procaryotic ribosomes.
Euglena EF-11 is the first EF-11 to be purified that functions on procaryotes and organelle ribosomes in addition to eukaryotes.
the EF-2s from Euglena are very different from those found in other organisms.
